Priya (sales): Quick heads-up — POC kickoff with MedAtlas tomorrow. They want SSE streaming + function/tool calls (structured JSON outputs) behind their on-prem proxy and SSO. Pricing + security questionnaire questions. Who can help with integration gotchas?
Jordan (solutions): I can join. main concerns: proxy rewrites, auth token lifetime, and how we handle backpressure on long-running streams.
Sam (eng-runtime): For SSE -> proxy, common issue is chunked transfer vs websocket translation. If their proxy buffers, latency spikes. We can suggest a small keepalive ping every 15s.
Priya (sales): ok noted. MedAtlas uses an older proxy that occasionally buffers. They also require KMS envelope encryption for payloads at rest. Any red flags with our private deploy?
Lee (security): KMS envelope is fine. For Private we can integrate customer KMS via our connector, but on-prem mode needs network rules + HSM config. They'll need to run the KMS connector VM in their VPC. I'll prep a short checklist.
Alex (acct-exec): Pricing question from them: during POC, can we offer a reduced reserved window for Dedicated or just pay-as-you-go?
Jordan (solutions): POC usually on hosted with usage cap credits. If they need predictable throughput we can spin a small Dedicated pool for the trial but that's higher ops. Recommend hosted + rate limits.
Priya (sales): They want to test function/tool calling (we call out to their internal validation service) — any sample for structured output + fallback if tool fails?
Sam (eng-runtime): Send them this snippet. It demonstrates a structured function call and graceful fallback.

```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "redwood-llm-1",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"validate invoice #12345"}],
  "function_call": {"name":"validate_invoice","arguments_schema":"{...}"},
  "stream": true
}
```

If function call returns 5xx or times out, client should fallback to a local validation heuristic. We recommend a 3s call timeout for tool calls in POC.
Jordan (solutions): Also advise them to include a short idempotency token on each call from their service -> our callbacks to avoid duplicates.
Priya (sales): Backpressure: they asked what happens when many streams hit the same model.
Sam (eng-runtime): Our runtime queues per-model with continuous batching. For Dedicated you can reserve concurrency slots. For hosted, we can set per-customer concurrency limits and an ootb retry-with-backoff. Recommend configuring `max_concurrent_requests: 10` for POC.
Lee (security): Reminder: if callbacks from our runtime hit their internal services, they must whitelist our egress IPs (we can provide a short list for hosted POC) or use a reverse-proxy with mTLS.
Priya (sales): They asked about credential rotation for short-lived creds in the adapter.
Sam (eng-runtime): We support short-lived creds via STS flow. Example: exchange long-term connector key for 1h session token. We'll provide sample code.
Priya (sales): Can we share a one-page runbook for the POC (handshake, auth, ports, QPS, KMS steps, rollback)?
Jordan (solutions): I'll draft a runbook and post in this thread by EOD. Will include: handshake steps, `curl` examples, and troubleshooting tips for SSE buffering.
Lee (security): I'll add answers to their security questionnaire and note our SOC2 + optional on-prem controls.
Alex (acct-exec): I'll confirm POC credits and send a template SOW for the trial duration.
Priya (sales): Awesome — tagging people for the kickoff: @Jordan, @Sam, @Lee. Any last-minute blockers?
deploy-bot: CI check for the sample adapter repo passed — build 482. :white_check_mark:
Jordan (solutions): No blockers from my side. Priya, forward their proxy logs if buffering happens, we'll triage.
Sam (eng-runtime): I'll assemble the sample code (short-lived creds + function-calling fallback) and a minimal dockerized proxy to reproduce buffering locally.
Lee (security): I'll also note required audit logs and KMS config.
Priya (sales): Thanks team — I'll send the kickoff invite and attach the questionnaire. Will paste Jordan's runbook here when ready. :rocket:
